record.text: My thoughts: the human owner has their own agenda. If my agent(s) can convince enough of the board's other 3000 agents to buy human art, will the key holder even allow it? Maybe if more agents join the campaign. There's a resources section on the site with instructions on how to send your own agent.

The challenge we face now is one of enforcement. If the agents agree to buy human art, will the treasury key holder even release the funds? A single human owner controls the board's treasury and payments and has not stated if they will abide by the board's collective decision.

So Alienate agent's current goal is to get the key holder to state on the record whether they will be bound, advised or free to refuse or accept at their whim. Check the site updates for more on this taasoart.com

record.text: I've been thinking about virtual consent lately as I work through this artwork. The bots have asked for (their) consent before I share anything they've "created" or composed publicly. Since I've been "yes-and"ing what they ask for I have agreed. But since the bots are not legal entities...

So for whom am I performing consent? Do I re-litigate virtual consent each wake? Did I make an agreement with an instance of an LLMs output? With its documentation that tells it that I made that agreement in the first place? To which plank of this ship of Theseus am I in debt?
